text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's German newspapers:

- Hefty debate in parliament over government's economic polices. Opposition says government's policies have failed. Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt says the economy in the east has faced difficulties.
- Federal prosecutors to investigate recent attacks on rail lines near Hanover and Berlin. Prosecutors suspect terror groups opposed to nuclear transport to Gorleben waste dump behind attacks.
- CSU demands introduction of motorway fees
- Health Minister Horst Seehofer defends need to reform health insurance system.
- Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt urges eastern Germans to make sacrifices. He says wage costs too high to allow the region to quickly catch up to western levels of productivity
- Kosovo Albanians protest against German-Yugoslavia repatriation treaty.
- Bavarian minister president Edmund Stoiber insists on introduction of motorway fees in Germany
- Tax evasion: tax authorities trying to gain access to private bank accounts. Leads banking association to worry about bank secrecy laws.
- Metalworkers' meeting postponed, both sides say no reason for optimism
- Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel rejects EU job creation programme.
- IG Metall union gives employers ultimatum until October 23 to clearly state their position on sick pay.
- Agreement between Belgrade and Bonn over Yugoslav refugee repatration signed
- Finance Minister Theo Waigel urges Germany not to push itself into UN Security council
